messages:
Avery (CEO): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime segment. I know we got a lot of great Qs about batching, caching, and kernel work. Starting a catch-all thread for lingering questions and action items. Please @Rohit for timeline/priority items.

Maya (Eng Manager): Can we summarize which runtime items are going into the next two sprints vs longer-term research?

Rohit (VP Eng): Short version: next 2 sprints = stability and incremental perf wins (KV cache bug fixes, safer batching heuristic, monitoring improvements). Research lane = attention fusion, alternative matmul paths, and broad kernel refactors — prototype/bench this quarter, rollout next quarter if stable.

Jon (Runtime): For clarity: KV cache invalidation when prompts truncate is the immediate bug. PR in review: rw-kv-271. Canary planned for next week.

Linh (ML Infra): Addendum: our attention fusion prototype shows ~10–15% throughput gains on long sequences in our lab runs, but it increases register pressure on older GPUs and needs more testing. It remains in R&D for now.

Camille (Product): How will this affect hosted vs Dedicated customers? Any special handling?

Rohit (VP Eng): Hosted: staged rollouts with automatic fallback to a compatible model/quantization variant. Dedicated: opt-in beta for customers who want early access; SE-assisted rollouts with a migration checklist.

Maya (Eng Manager): Practically speaking customers should see no disruptions. Expected outcome: slightly lower p50 for steady workloads; watch p95 for tiny, bursty requests until we tune heuristics.

Avery (CEO): Any known regressions we should proactively communicate?

Jon (Runtime): We saw a small tail increase for very small requests when the batch-window is increased. Mitigation: keep small-request heuristic enabled (requests <32 tokens bypass long-window batching).

Linh (ML Infra): Also, attention-fusion benefits start showing up beyond ~1024 tokens. We should gate that path by model profile to avoid regressions on short-seq models.

Maya (Eng Manager): Ops rollout plan: canary (24h) -> verify SLIs -> stage rollout -> global. SLIs: token-level p50/p95 latency, error rate, tokens/sec.

Rohit (VP Eng): Timeline bullets: KV fixes -> canary next week. Safer batching heuristic -> targeted rollout over 2 sprints. Attention fusion -> prototype this quarter, broad rollout early next quarter pending stability.

Camille (Product): Can we give SEs a short runbook to answer customer inquiries?

Jon (Runtime): I'll draft a 1-pager covering what changed, expected impact, edge cases, and how Dedicated customers can opt out.

Maya (Eng Manager): I'll make a short FAQ for the Console: how to detect if your workload benefits, and recommended toggles.

Avery (CEO): If a customer hits a regression, escalate to incidents and tag me.

Rohit (VP Eng): For folks experimenting locally, a dev snippet (dev-only flags):

```
# dev-only runtime flags
./serve --kv-cache=on --batch-window-ms=10 --batch-size-max=192
# if you see tail latency on tiny requests try:
./serve --small-request-heuristic=on --batch-window-ms=2
```

Jon (Runtime): Reminder: those flags are for local/dev clusters only. Don't flip them in hosted prod.

Linh (ML Infra): Q from infra: do quantization profiles need updates? Short answer: one new profile for attention-fused kernels; we keep existing quant paths as fallback. Minimal customer-visible change expected.

Camille (Product): Any cost implications?

Rohit (VP Eng): Net: long-seq workloads should see token compute reductions due to better kernel efficiency. Short-batch workloads might see small compute uptick if batch-window is extended; we'll set safe defaults to avoid cost regressions.

Maya (Eng Manager): Follow-ups I'm owning: 1) Runbook + FAQ 2) Canary dashboard + explainer 3) Post-rollout perf dashboard.

Avery (CEO): Good. Camille/SEs, if Dedicated customers ask for early access, coordinate with Runtime + SE checklist.

Camille (Product): One customer asked if Dedicated customers could opt into attention fusion early. Answer: yes, on a vetted beta basis.

Jon (Runtime): I'll post the SE checklist: tests to run, key metrics, rollback criteria.

Avery (CEO): OK closing in 24h unless someone objects. Move unresolved items into the runtime roadmap epic. :tada:

deploy-bot: Canary started for rw-kv-271 in us-west-2-canary. CI run: https://ci.internal.redwood/run/9921

Maya (Eng Manager): Seeing the canary. I'm watching p95; ping me if >180ms.

Jon (Runtime): Early canary: p50 -7%, p95 steady. Will update in 6h.

Linh (ML Infra): I'll attach perf artifacts to the epic.

Camille (Product): Adding SE contact list to the epic.

Avery (CEO): Thanks everyone.
